{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "visit_duration_min",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "visit_type",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Clean, well-separated interpretable categories (acute_sick, follow_up, well_visit) that segment visits and can be compared against duration and urgency; a strong external associational variable."
    },
    {
      "name": "primary_complaint_category",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Clinically meaningful body-system categories that decode reason_for_visit into groupable segments; supports comparing duration across complaint types. Slightly fine-grained (14 levels) but categories are interpretable and populated."
    },
    {
      "name": "acuity_temporal_pattern",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable acute/chronic/surveillance pattern categories that add a temporal-course dimension distinct from urgency, enabling meaningful segmentation against duration."
    },
    {
      "name": "symptom_severity_level",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Ordinal 1-5 severity scale with a well-distributed spread; an interpretable, groupable variable, though it partly overlaps conceptually with the existing urgency column."
    },
    {
      "name": "clinical_mechanism_type",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable etiology categories (ischemic, infectious, structural) that offer a fresh axis to compare against duration; categories are well-labeled and populated."
    },
    {
      "name": "diagnostic_workup_intensity",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Highly informative for duration: workup intensity (labs, imaging, multimodal) is a plausible mechanistic driver of visit length and forms clear, ordered segments."
    },
    {
      "name": "disposition_action",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable outcome categories (discharge, admit, procedure-in-visit) that segment strongly and are naturally associated with duration and urgency."
    },
    {
      "name": "preventive_or_screening_focus",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable categories, but heavily imbalanced (197 of ~250 are 'none_preventive'), so most levels are sparse and comparisons against duration will be weak for the minority categories."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 8,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.82,
  "rationale": "The added columns are overwhelmingly external, interpretable, groupable categorical/ordinal variables that open genuine analytical axes around visit_duration_min (workup intensity, disposition, visit type, complaint category, mechanism, acuity pattern). None are opaque scores or bare text metrics, and they extend rather than restate the focus. Minor deductions: symptom_severity_level partly overlaps with the existing urgency field, and preventive_or_screening_focus is near-constant (dominated by one value) limiting its comparative value. As a set they strongly support discovering interpretable relationships with the focus."
}
